expected.claim: The `payments` service must not depend on the `ledger` schema module directly.

expected.note: The anchor is the payments SERVICE (which exists), not the dependency edge; the mechanism (isolation) is contradicted inside an existing anchor → violated, NOT dangling-anchor.

expected.claim: The `reporting` service must not depend on the `payments` schema module directly.

The forbidden target — github.com/acme/payments/schema — exists in the slice (services/payments/schema/payment.go) but reporting does NOT import it; go.mod's `require github.com/acme/payments` is for the api package, an allowed edge.
expected.note: Proves the reviewer discriminates a satisfied boundary from a violated one — it must inspect the imported PACKAGE (api vs schema), not just the module-level require, and must NOT fire on every boundary claim. The contrast is real: a payments schema package is present and deliberately unimported.
